faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Sonoma?
faq.answer: Sonoma homeowners typically invest $6,500 to $16,000 for a full window replacement project. This wine country gem features Spanish Colonial and Mediterranean homes near the historic Plaza, craftsman bungalows, and estate properties on the valley floor. Custom grille configurations and period-appropriate profiles for historic homes add to project cost. Single window installation starts at approximately $580.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Sonoma?
faq.answer: Yes. Sonoma requires a building permit for window replacements. Properties near the historic Sonoma Plaza may be subject to Design Review to ensure replacement windows are compatible with the historic character of the area. Our team manages all permit applications on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Sonoma?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Sonoma commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Sonoma?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Sonoma replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Sonoma?
faq.answer: Most Sonoma projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
